items.title: “What Have You Awakened?” — Madison Darkwave Artist Carrellee Shares Video for “Waiting” Ahead of European Tour With Bragolin
items.summary: What have you awakened? Cuz I’m already already gone Sometimes you catch yourself talking about a place in the past tense while you’re still sitting in it. Your coat is… The post “What Have You Awakened?” — Madison Darkwave Artist Carrellee Shares Video for “W
items.fullText:
What have you awakened?
Cuz I’m already already gone

Sometimes you catch yourself talking about a place in the past tense while you’re still sitting in it. Your coat is on the hook and the sunlight falls across the wall at its usual hour, but you’ve rehearsed leaving so often that the room has begun to feel like a memory. In Waiting, Madison, Wisconsin darkwave artist Carrellee weighs the time she’s lost to worry against the risk of putting her heart on the line again. She asks what someone has awakened in her and hears herself answer that she’s already gone. The second “already” sounds like the moment she realizes she means it.

The bass is already moving when she starts to sing. A springy synth figure doubles back on itself before the kick lands, and rippling synths gather behind her as bell tones ring between lines. Carrellee keeps her voice close, with the silky composure of Curve’s Toni Halliday and some of the frank sensuality of Sinéad O’Connor’s “I Want Your (Hands on Me).” The synth layers have the glossy sweep of Madonna’s Ray of Light.

Carrellee made that turn toward late-’90s and early-’00s techno and dance pop in Madison, where she wrote, performed, and produced the single. She brought back Maurizio Baggio (The Soft Moon, Boy Harsher) to mix and Josh Bonati (Adrianne Lenker) to master. Both worked on her self-titled 2025 album for Young & Cold Records.

Carrellee shot and directed the video herself, too, giving it the close framing and everyday details of a home movie. She lies among fallen leaves, sings beside a backyard grill with the wind pushing her hair across her eyes, and stretches her arms wide in front of shelves packed with records. By the water, the sun turns her into a silhouette. When the camera returns to the leaves, the ground is empty, as though the image has finally caught up with the refrain.

Watch the video for “Waiting” below.

Carrellee spent years performing as a folk artist before she turned to darkwave. Her 2022 debut, Scale of Dreams, sold out its first pressing on Negative Gain Productions, and No Coast Records put it back in print. She took those songs to Chicago’s Cold Waves, Vancouver’s Verboden, and a Synthicide night at Brooklyn’s Saint Vitus. On Rescaled, she handed them over to remixers including Patriarchy, Casket Cassette, and former Smashing Pumpkins guitarist Jeff Schroeder.

Touring brought her to IAMX, first as an opener in the Midwest in 2023 and then as a backing vocalist and synth player on European and North American dates in 2024 and 2025. Back in the studio, she brought in Matia Simovich and Ryan McCambridge for additional production on her self-titled second album. The record gave her a breakout single in “Captain,” earned airplay on KEXP, and reached the top ten of the Deutsche Alternative Charts. IAMX, INHALT, and Bragolin later reworked songs from it for a remix EP.

In 2026, Carrellee headlined a 30-date U.S. tour and returned to Verboden. Her collaboration with Bragolin extended beyond the remix. She sang on “Feel This Flame Unfold” from the Dutch darkwave project’s I Don’t Like What It Does to Me, and the labelmates co-headlined a North American run this fall. Carrellee will open for Bragolin on all 21 dates of their next run, which starts November 12 at Glasgow’s Ivory Blacks and marks her first European tour under the Carrellee name.

“Waiting” is out now. Order the single on Bandcamp.

items.title: Mari Kattman releases new single ‘It’s In The Losing You’ via Metropolis Records
items.summary: US musician Mari Kattman releases "It's In The Losing You" via Metropolis Records on November 6, 2026, following her 2025 album "Year Of The Katt".
items.fullText:
US electronic musician and vocalist Mari Kattman has released her new single, “It’s In The Losing You”, today, November 6, 2026, through Metropolis Records.

Written and produced by Kattman herself, the track combines synth-pop, EBM and industrial influences with driving electronic beats and her distinctive vocals. Lyrically, it deals with self-worth, letting go of expectations and finally refusing to seek validation from others.

Kattman explains the idea behind the song:

“It’s about the liberation that comes with finally saying fuck it and realising that the validation you’ve spent a lifetime seeking was never someone else’s to give. Your worth is determined by the one constant – yourself.”

The single follows her 2025 album “Year Of The Katt”, her first full-length release for Metropolis Records. The album featured tracks such as “Anemia”, “Sharp Shooter” and “Typical Girl”.

Active as a musician, songwriter and producer since 2012, Kattman has built an extensive list of collaborations, including work with Mesh, Rotersand, Neuroticfish, Comaduster and Caustic.

More recently, she contributed vocals to “Ich Will Nur Das”, a September 2026 single by Lords Of Acid, released ahead of their album “Mundo Bizarro”.

Kattman has also been confirmed for the 2027 edition of M’era Luna Festival in Hildesheim, Germany.

“It’s In The Losing You” is available now on streaming platforms and Bandcamp.

Mari Kattman on self-worth and letting go

“It’s In The Losing You” follows Kattman’s own account of the song’s theme: a refusal to keep seeking validation from others after a lifetime of doing so. The track keeps the electro-industrial sound of her other work, built this time around the idea that self-worth does not depend on anyone else’s approval.

About Mari Kattman

Mari Kattman is a musician, songwriter, producer and vocalist based in Boston, Massachusetts, self-recording, composing, producing and performing live since 2012. Her work combines synth-pop, EBM and industrial influences, and she has built a wide list of collaborations across the electronic music scene, including with Mesh, Rotersand, Neuroticfish, Comaduster and Caustic.

In 2025, Kattman announced her debut full-length for Metropolis Records, “Year Of The Katt”, and shared a video for “Typical Girl” ahead of its release. The album included tracks such as “Anemia” and “Sharp Shooter” alongside “Typical Girl”. Side-Line interviewed Kattman around the album’s release.

Kattman has also toured as part of Assemblage 23’s 2026 European headline run, and contributed vocals to Lords Of Acid’s “Ich Will Nur Das”, released ahead of their album “Mundo Bizarro”.

“It’s In The Losing You”, released November 6, 2026 via Metropolis Records, is Kattman’s latest single after “Year Of The Katt” and her Assemblage 23 and Lords Of Acid collaborations, and she is confirmed to perform at the 2027 edition of M’era Luna Festival in Hildesheim, Germany.

items.title: j:dead closes year-long single campaign with ‘XVII’
items.summary: UK industrial-electronic artist j:dead closes a year-long single campaign with "XVII", released November 6, 2026 via Infacted Recordings.
items.fullText:
UK industrial-electronic artist j:dead has released “XVII” on November 6, 2026 via Infacted Recordings, closing a year-long single campaign that began in December 2025 with “Pressure”.

“XVII” is built around distorted guitar riffs and mid-tempo drums, wrapped in warm, expressive vocals over an industrial base. Instead of closing the campaign with another explosive statement, the track turns inward toward a more measured conclusion.

The song moves between childhood and adulthood, viewing the hopes and dreams of a young man through the perspective of an older self who has lived through more and understands the distance between the person he imagined becoming and the person he became. The title refers to the age of seventeen, the final year of the life j:dead describes before his own story began.

“XVII” was written, performed and recorded by j:dead (Jay Taylor), with guitars by Hilger Tintel and Jay Taylor. Motel-Music produced the track and Studio-600 handled mastering; the artwork is by Dokodemo.

“XVII” is available now on Bandcamp and streaming platforms.

The twelfth single in j:dead’s year-long campaign

j:dead launched the campaign in December 2025 with “Pressure”, followed by “Who Knows” as the third single in January 2026 and a video for “Feeling Alone” in March 2026. Later entries included “Keep Walking”, “Draws My Blood”, “Halo”, “Null” and “Cannibal”, each one released on Infacted Recordings through 2026. “XVII” closes the series as its twelfth and final single.

About j:dead

j:dead is the project of UK musician Jay Taylor. The project makes industrial-electronic music built around distorted guitars, programmed rhythms and emotionally direct songwriting. The project’s catalog includes the singles “Haunt” (2019) and “Feeding On Me” (2020), the album “A Complicated Genocide” (2021), the collaboration “Tearing Me Apart” with Teknovore (2021) and the single “I’ll Wait” (2021).

Further releases followed with the “DAS OM3N” cover single (2022), the “Vision Of Time” EP (2022), “Hold Tight” with remixes (2022), the collaborations “High Time (Chinese Takeaway)” with FabrikC and “Thrive” with Nature Of Wires (both 2022), “Surrendering” with remixes (2023), the “You Spin Me Round (Like a Record)” cover single with Menschdefekt (2023), “Harbour” (2023), the “ROOTS” EP (2023) and the single “What We’ll Be” (2024).

In December 2025, j:dead signed to Infacted Recordings and opened a year-long single campaign with “Pressure”, followed through 2026 by “Disgusting”, “Who Knows”, “Feeling Alone”, “Silence Calls”, “Over The Years”, “Keep Walking”, “Draws My Blood”, “Halo”, “Null” and “Cannibal”. “XVII”, released November 6, 2026, closes that campaign as its twelfth single.

items.title: “Paris te brutalise, t’immortalise” — French Post-Punk Artist Anton Unveils Video for “Serpent Des Villes”
items.summary: Paris te brutalise, t’immortalise Te brutalise, t’immortalise A city can bruise you and still be the place you most want to remember your name. Paris makes that bargain especially seductive.… The post “Paris te brutalise, t’immortalise” — French Post-Punk Arti
items.fullText:
Paris te brutalise, t’immortalise
Te brutalise, t’immortalise

A city can bruise you and still be the place you most want to remember your name. Paris makes that bargain especially seductive. You go there to become someone, then spend half your time figuring out how to dress, speak, and carry yourself so nobody can tell how badly you want to belong. In Anton’s Serpent Des Villes, black rain comes down, and the city lights go out. By then, Paris has already exacted its tribute. It has taught you to keep up appearances even in the dark.

“Paris te brutalise, t’immortalise,” sings Anton Steinbock. Paris brutalizes you, Paris immortalizes you, and the ease with which one verb follows the other makes the promise sound like a threat. Then comes the refrain, “Y’a rien de pire qu’être parfait” (there’s nothing worse than being perfect), repeated until it sounds as much like a private admonition as a public accusation. Out November 6, “Serpent Des Villes” is the first single from Anton’s forthcoming EP, Tôt Ou Tard.

An organ-like synth picks out a bright, clipped melody over a lower electronic throb and the dry crunch of the drum machine. The French new wave inflection is there before Steinbock sings a word. His voice glides over the beat, giving the French vowels room to stretch while wiry post-punk guitars answer at the ends of his lines. About two-thirds of the way through, the arrangement takes a breath and a rippling bass synth comes forward, giving the song a loose-hipped shuffle on its way to the final refrain. It’s a trick French coldwave has long made its own. The tune is so inviting you catch yourself singing along before you’ve reckoned with the words.

The video finds Steinbock alone in a park, where two crows pick over the lawn and branches fill the frame. He paces, turns with his arms flung out, and brings a hand to his face. From a bench beneath the trees, he sings with the same agitation that sends him back onto the path. By the end, the camera looks up at him against a grey sky and his face is nearly lost in silhouette. He has room to move here, though the urgency of his gestures suggests that getting away from the city and getting it out of your head are two very different things.

Watch the video for Serpent Des Villes below.

Steinbock launched Anton as a solo darkwave project in Paris in 2024, drawing on bands like Joy Division and Lebanon Hanover while singing in French, German, and English. His debut EP Volcan came out that May on Detriti Records, and Anton’s initial live quartet shared bills with TRAITRS, Nürnberg, and Sad Madona. Icy Cold Records issued Glacier / Volcan in March 2025, featuring the standout “L’Autre Destination”. Artist Sylvester Engbrox provided the album artwork and also worked on the videos for the double single Never Freed Myself. Anton played its first international dates in Italy at the end of 2025. The project now performs as a duo, with Steinbock on bass and vocals and artist Gabriela Guyez on synths and vocals.

items.title: OMD’s ‘Architecture & Morality’ turns 45 on 6 November
items.summary: OMD's "Architecture & Morality" turns 45 on 6 November 2026. The 1981 Dindisc album produced the UK top-5 singles "Souvenir" and "Maid of Orleans".
items.fullText:
OMD’s third studio album, “Architecture & Morality”, turns 45 on 6 November. Orchestral Manoeuvres in the Dark released the record through Dindisc on 6 November 1981, recording it over two months at the Gramophone Suite in Liverpool, the Manor Studio in Shipton-on-Cherwell and Mayfair Studios in London. Richard Manwaring produced the album with the band and Mike Howlett, and its nine tracks run 37 minutes.

Three UK top-5 singles from ‘Architecture & Morality’

The album carried OMD from new-wave outsiders into the UK singles chart. “Souvenir”, issued on 21 August 1981, reached number 3. “Joan of Arc” followed on 16 October 1981 and peaked at number 5, and “Maid of Orleans (The Waltz Joan of Arc)” came out on 15 January 1982 and climbed to number 4, going on to become Germany’s best-selling single of 1982. The three singles sold a combined 8 million copies. “Architecture & Morality” itself peaked at number 3 on the UK Albums Chart, topped the Dutch chart and reached number 8 in Germany and number 144 on the US Billboard 200, with worldwide sales passing 4 million copies; the album holds Platinum certification in the UK and Spain and Gold in the Netherlands.

The tracklist runs: “The New Stone Age”, “She’s Leaving”, “Souvenir”, “Sealand”, “Joan of Arc”, “Joan of Arc (Maid of Orleans)”, “Architecture and Morality”, “Georgia” and “The Beginning and the End”. Designer Peter Saville, working with Brett Wickens, created the sleeve, and the album’s title comes from “Morality and Architecture”, a 1977 book by David Watkin.

OMD released a dedicated singles reissue for the album’s 40th anniversary in 2021, and the band has returned to the record on stage, performing “Architecture & Morality” in full alongside “Dazzle Ships” at the Royal Albert Hall in London.

About OMD

Andy McCluskey (vocals, bass) and Paul Humphreys (keyboards, vocals) formed OMD in September 1978 in Meols, on the Wirral Peninsula in England, renaming their side project VCL XI to Orchestral Manoeuvres in the Dark. Both had played together in the seven-piece band The Id, whose members included drummer Malcolm Holmes. OMD debuted live in October 1978 at Eric’s Club in Liverpool and released its first single, “Electricity”, through Factory Records, which led to a seven-album deal with Dindisc worth more than 250,000 pounds.

Holmes and keyboardist and saxophonist Martin Cooper joined in 1980, forming OMD’s classic line-up for the self-titled debut album and “Organisation”, both released that year behind the singles “Messages” and “Enola Gay”. “Architecture & Morality” followed in 1981 as the band’s commercial breakthrough. OMD continued with “Dazzle Ships” (1983), “Junk Culture” (1984), “Crush” (1985) and “The Pacific Age” (1986) before Humphreys, Cooper and Holmes left in 1989 to form The Listening Pool, leaving McCluskey to continue OMD alone through “Sugar Tax” (1991), “Liberator” (1993) and “Universal” (1996), after which the band went on hiatus.

McCluskey and Humphreys reformed OMD in 2006 with Holmes and Cooper, and the band has since released “History of Modern” (2010), “English Electric” (2013), “The Punishment of Luxury” (2017) and “Bauhaus Staircase” (2023). Side-Line has covered the band’s catalogue reissues of “Dazzle Ships”, “Junk Culture” and “Crush”, as well as “Universal” turning 30 earlier this year. “Architecture & Morality”, the record that turned OMD into a chart act, turns 45 on 6 November.

items.title: Adam and the Ants’ ‘Prince Charming’ turns 45 on 6 November
items.summary: Adam and the Ants' "Prince Charming" turns 45 on 6 November. CBS Records released the album on 6 November 1981, produced by Chris Hughes.
items.fullText:
Adam and the Ants’ “Prince Charming” turns 45 this year. The English new wave band released the album through CBS Records on 6 November 1981, the follow-up to its UK number-one “Kings of the Wild Frontier” from the previous year.

Chris Hughes, who also played drums in the band, produced “Prince Charming.” The original LP and cassette carried ten tracks across two sides: “Scorpios,” “Picasso Visita El Planeta De Los Simios,” “Prince Charming,” “Five Guns West” and “That Voodoo!” opened side one, followed by “Stand and Deliver,” “Mile High Club,” “Ant Rap,” “Mowhok” and “S.E.X.” on side two. The album reached number two on the UK Albums Chart, held off the top spot for three weeks.

Three singles came from the album cycle. “Stand and Deliver,” issued 1 May 1981, became the band’s first UK number one and stayed there for five weeks. The title track “Prince Charming” followed on 4 September 1981, also reaching number one, for four weeks. “Ant Rap” came last, released 4 December 1981 and peaking at number three after a remix the following January.

The album is available to stream on Spotify as a remastered edition that adds six demo recordings to the original ten-track sequence.

About Adam and the Ants

Adam and the Ants formed in London in May 1977 around Stuart Leslie Goddard, who performed as Adam Ant, with guitarist Lester Square, bassist Andy Warren and drummer Paul Flanagan. The group used the name The Ants before settling on Adam and the Ants that November. Square left to finish an art course and was replaced by Mark Ryan, who was later succeeded by Johnny Bivouac, while Dave Barbarossa took over on drums from Flanagan.

Early singles appeared on Decca (“Young Parisians,” October 1978) and Do It Records (“Zerox,” July 1979), and the band contributed to the “Jubilee” film soundtrack in 1978. The debut album, “Dirk Wears White Sox,” followed in 1979 and reached number one on the UK Independent Albums Chart, recorded by a lineup of Adam Ant, Matthew Ashman, Leigh Gorman and Barbarossa. In January 1980, manager Malcolm McLaren persuaded Ashman, Gorman and Barbarossa to leave and form Bow Wow Wow, leaving Adam Ant as the only remaining member.

A new lineup took shape from February 1980: guitarist Marco Pirroni, who became Adam Ant’s principal co-writer, bassist Kevin Mooney, and drummers Terry Lee Miall and Chris Hughes. Mooney was replaced by Gary Tibbs in February 1981. The band signed to CBS Records in July 1980 and built its sound around Burundi-style tribal drumming, paired with pirate and Native American-influenced costumes and makeup associated with the New Romantic movement. “Kings of the Wild Frontier,” released in November 1980, reached number one on the UK Albums Chart in January 1981 behind the singles “Antmusic,” “Dog Eat Dog” and the title track.

“Prince Charming” followed on 6 November 1981, peaked at number two in the UK, and was promoted with the Prince Charming Revue tour through Austria and Japan that September. The band earned a Grammy nomination for Best New Artist in 1982, and Adam Ant and Pirroni won an Ivor Novello Award for Songwriter of the Year for “Stand and Deliver.” Adam Ant disbanded the group in March 1982 and continued working with Pirroni on a solo career that opened with the UK number-one single “Goody Two Shoes.” “Prince Charming,” the band’s last album before the split, turns 45 on 6 November.

items.title: 808 Dot Pop releases architectural ‘neofuturism EP’
items.summary: 808 Dot Pop, the solo project of Metroland's Passenger S, releases the 3-track "neofuturism EP" on Alfa Matrix, ahead of the "Maximalism" album.
items.fullText:
Belgian electronic pop project 808 Dot Pop has released the “neofuturism EP”, a 3-track digital release, via Alfa Matrix on November 6, 2026. The project is the solo outlet of Passenger S, also of Metroland, and the new EP continues the architectural concept the act has built its recent releases around.

The EP’s three tracks each pair an architectural style with the building that inspired it: “neofuturism (l’hemisfèric)” (2:47), named for the Valencia arts complex; “purism (maison guiette)” (5:27), named for Le Corbusier’s Antwerp house; and “neofuturism (space needle)” (6:28), named for the Space Needle in Seattle. The same “neofuturism” and “purism” names, paired with different buildings, appear on the track lists of 808 Dot Pop’s forthcoming albums “Minimalism” and “Maximalism”, due on Alfa Matrix on November 30, 2026.

“neofuturism EP” is available as a digital EP on Bandcamp. Recommend to fans of Kraftwerk, Komputer and Orbital.

‘neofuturism EP’ extends 808 Dot Pop’s architectural series

The EP follows the “minimalism EP” digital single, released on September 25, 2026 ahead of the “Minimalism” and “Maximalism” albums. Those two companion records carry 18 tracks between them, each named after an architectural “ism” and a specific building, with the label describing “Minimalism” as the project’s “white album” and “Maximalism” as its “black album” counterpart.

About 808 Dot Pop

808 Dot Pop is the solo electronic pop project of Belgian producer Passenger S, who also records as Metroland. Passenger S launched 808 Dot Pop in March 2020 with the debut album “The Colour Temperature” and its companion remix album “The Cubic Temperature”. The project returned in March 2023 with three albums in one go (“AM 1350” and “FM 88.2” on CD, “MW 720” digitally), followed by a double EP that June. In September 2026, 808 Dot Pop announced the twin albums “Minimalism” and “Maximalism”, a concept built around 20th-century architecture, preceded by the “minimalism EP” single.

The “neofuturism EP” extends that architectural concept with new building-inspired versions of “neofuturism” and “purism”, ahead of the two albums’ release on November 30, 2026.

items.title: Aesthetische releases ‘Mix The State’ remix EP
items.summary: Brazilian EBM duo Aesthetische releases the 4-track "Mix The State" EP on Alfa Matrix, built around two new versions of "Break The State".
items.fullText:
Brazilian EBM duo Aesthetische has released “Mix The State”, a 4-track remix EP, via Alfa Matrix on November 6, 2026. The digital-only EP is built around “Break The State”, a track from Aesthetische’s “Every Beat Matters” EP, and adds two reworked versions alongside a previously unreleased instrumental.

The EP opens with the “static noise version” of “Break The State” (4:36), which pushes the track into a noisier, more industrial register, followed by “Alarmstate” (3:25), an instrumental built for club play with no vocals. The “electric hell version” of “Break The State” (4:30) raises the track’s electronic intensity, and the EP closes with the original “Break The State” (4:16). “Mix The State” is available as a digital EP on Bandcamp.

Aesthetische ties the EP to the classic EBM tradition of Front 242 and Front Line Assembly, while applying a harder, contemporary production approach.

Aesthetische reworks ‘Break The State’ for ‘Mix The State’

“Mix The State” expands a single track from “Every Beat Matters” into a four-version release, pairing the two new mixes with the unreleased “Alarmstate” and the original recording.

About Aesthetische

Aesthetische is a Brazilian EBM and industrial duo formed by Gui Pires and Fab Viscardi in 2012, after both previously worked together in Aghast View and Biopsy, a Brazilian electro-industrial act active in the 1990s. The duo signed to Belgian label Alfa Matrix in 2012 and has released albums, EPs and digital singles through the label since, including the albums “Powerswitch” (2012), “HybridCore” (2014), “Co3xist3ns3” (2019) and “Rvprty” (2022), plus a run of EPs and singles that includes “Boiling Over” (2023), “Confidence Is Silent” (2024) and the 6-track EPCD “Selling Fear” (2025). Aesthetische also appeared on the 2012 split EP “4.4U [2012.11]” alongside Metroland, Mentallo & The Fixer and Daniel B. Prothèse.

“Mix The State” returns to “Every Beat Matters”, reworking “Break The State” into two new versions and adding the previously unreleased “Alarmstate” to the duo’s Alfa Matrix catalog.

items.title: Acylum releases reinterpretation album ‘XXI21XXI’
items.summary: German dark electro act Acylum releases "XXI21XXI" on Alfa Matrix on November 6, 2026, a 10-track follow-up to last year's "XX20XX" anniversary album.
items.fullText:
German dark electro project Acylum has released “XXI21XXI” via Alfa Matrix on November 6, 2026. The 10-track digital album follows XX20XX, the 20th-anniversary reinterpretation album Acylum released through the same label in December 2025, and continues the project’s run of reworking its own back catalog.

Where “XX20XX” focused on reconstruction, “XXI21XXI” pushes the same eight source tracks further, with Pedro and Nadine Engel reworking the material into harder, more aggressive versions. The album opens with “Your Pain – XXI21XXI” (4:03) and “Sieg Oder Walhalla – XXI21XXI” (4:00), followed by “Romance – XXI21XXI” (3:06), “Alone – XXI21XXI” (4:14), “Kategorie C – XXI21XXI” (3:14), “The Rhythm Of Violence – XXI21XXI” (3:51) and “Masquerade – XXI21XXI” (3:16). “Waldgeist – XXI21XXI” (3:28) features Totem Obscura, and the album closes with two further versions of “Alone – XXI21XXI”: a remix by Diverje (5:12) and one by Nano Infect (4:17).

“XXI21XXI” is available as a digital album on Bandcamp.

‘XXI21XXI’ continues Acylum’s 21-year catalog

Acylum marks 21 years of activity with “XXI21XXI”. The label describes the release as a continuation of “XX20XX”: the same eight tracks return in sharper, more extreme form, with “Romance – XXI21XXI” and “Masquerade – XXI21XXI” set against the album’s harder material, and “Waldgeist – XXI21XXI” built around its Totem Obscura feature.

About Acylum

Acylum is a German dark electro and industrial project led by Pedro and Nadine Engel, active for 21 years as of this release. The project built a catalog of albums and EPs on Alfa Matrix, including the 2CD album Zuchthaus in April 2024, a remix from Wumpscut on the Kalashnikov download EP in March 2023, and an appearance on the “Ukraina” charity single alongside Aesthetische, Kant Kino and Cubic in December 2022. Side-Line interviewed the project in June 2021 and again in May 2024. In December 2025, Acylum marked its 20th anniversary with the reinterpretation album XX20XX on Alfa Matrix.

“XXI21XXI” follows directly from that anniversary album, taking the same eight-track core further into harsher, more extreme territory with the Totem Obscura feature and the closing Diverje and Nano Infect remixes of “Alone”.

items.title: Death Rights debuts with dark electro single ‘Crucify’
items.summary: Death Rights, a new dark electro project from members of Frontal Boundary and Protokoll 19, releases debut single "Crucify" on Alfa Matrix.
items.fullText:
Belgian label Alfa Matrix has released “Crucify”, the debut single from new dark electro act Death Rights, on November 6, 2026. The two-track digital single pairs the title track with a reworked cover of “Get Low” by Lil Jon & The East Side Boyz, and marks the project’s first transmission ahead of a debut album called “Interitio”.

Death Rights is built from members of Frontal Boundary and Protokoll 19, two acts already on the Alfa Matrix roster, combining dark electro, EBM and industrial into a sound the label describes as both mechanical and ritualistic. “Crucify” runs 4:17 and opens the single with pounding sequences, distorted vocals and dense electronic textures. “Get Low” closes it out at 4:40, transforming the original hip-hop track into a harsher, electro-industrial version.

Both songs are written by Brendin Ross and Travis Hines, with “Get Low” additionally crediting original writers Lil Jon and the Eastside Boyz. Lyrics and vocals come from Krz Greenhaw and Jayson Smith. Brendin Ross produced the single and handled mastering, and mixed it together with Krz Greenhaw. The cover artwork is by Vlad McNeally. “Crucify” is available as a digital single on Bandcamp.

Recommend to fans of Suicide Commando, Aslan Faction, Alien Vampires and C-Lekktor.

Death Rights’ debut single sets up album ‘Interitio’

The label describes “Crucify” as the first transmission from Death Rights. It sets out the oppressive, ritualistic territory the project plans to expand on its debut album, “Interitio”. No release date for the album has been announced.

About Death Rights

Death Rights is a new dark electro, EBM and industrial project formed from members of Frontal Boundary and Protokoll 19, both signed to Alfa Matrix. Frontal Boundary joined the label in July 2025 with the 3-track EP “Hate”, followed by the 8-track “Faith” EP that September, the 2CD album “Failure” in December 2025, an interview with Side-Line in January 2026, and the “Burn” EP in April 2026, which closed out the “Failure” cycle and included a cover of Filter’s “Hey Man Nice Shot”. Protokoll 19 released the single “Witch” in May 2024, the “Mental Decay” EP that July, and the singles “Connect” and “Trivialized” in May 2025.

Death Rights debuts on Alfa Matrix with “Crucify”, positioning the project within the label’s dark electro and EBM lineup alongside its two feeder acts, ahead of the forthcoming album “Interitio”.

items.title: Never Knows Best – Hell
items.summary: Gloomy synth pop from the US. Read my review to find out how Never Knows Best captivate listeners with their powerful basslines and versatile vocals.
items.fullText:
When synth pop embraces hell

With their song “Hell”, Never Knows Best deliv­er a dark synth pop track that clearly bears the hall­marks of dark wave and post-punk. The sound is crisp and pleas­antly bass-heavy, instantly cre­at­ing a dense atmo­sphere. I find the extremely var­ied vocals par­tic­u­larly fas­cin­at­ing; they lend the verses and the chor­us their own dis­tinct­ive, strik­ing character.

Lyrically, the song tackles themes such as self-doubt, emo­tion­al entan­gle­ments and self-imposed dark­ness, with lines like “Is this hell? We can’t find our way out / We built it ourselves” aptly reflect­ing a sense of being lost. Ultimately, this track builds on the atmo­spher­ic style that I’d already come to appre­ci­ate back in January with their release ‘Something From Nothing’, and seam­lessly main­tains that stand­ard. The res­ult is an extremely catchy synth pop track that had me hooked from the very first moment.

items.title: Nachtfalter announce third album ‘Still(Leben)’
items.summary: German dark rock band Nachtfalter will release its third album, "Still(Leben)," on November 6, 2026, via Echozone.
items.fullText:
German dark rock band Nachtfalter will release its third album, “Still(Leben)”, on November 6, 2026, via Echozone. The label describes the record as pairing hymnic black metal with somber dark rock, sung entirely in German.

Nachtfalter is the project of Tobias Serfling, who founded the band in Altenburg, Germany, in early 2017 after 30 years in other bands. The press has referred to the group’s style as “Dark Poetry Rock,” drawing comparisons to Witt, Lacrimosa and Rammstein. Ahead of “Still(Leben),” the band released three singles: “Bodenlos” in January 2026, “Als du gingst” in April 2026 and “Mottentanz” (“Moth Dance”) on September 25, 2026, the last accompanied by an official lyric video and available on major streaming platforms.

“Still(Leben)” follows Nachtfalter’s 2019 debut, “was bleibt,” whose lead single “Maschinenklang” spent six weeks in the German Alternative Charts while the album held a place in the Official German Metal & Rock Charts for more than eight weeks. The band’s second album, “Abschied” (2024), entered the DAC charts at number six behind lead single “Du bist mein,” and its track “Narbentage” reached the final round of Sonic Seducer magazine’s Battle of the Bands competition in 2023. Nachtfalter has been featured in Orkus, Sonic Seducer and Legacy magazines, and began performing live in 2025.

About Nachtfalter

Nachtfalter is a German dark rock and metal project founded by Tobias Serfling in Altenburg in early 2017, built around German-language lyrics and a style the press has called “Dark Poetry Rock.” The band’s debut album, “was bleibt” (2019, Echozone), and second album, “Abschied” (2024), both charted in Germany, and Nachtfalter began touring in 2025. Side-Line previously covered the band’s single “Als du gingst” in April 2026. The group’s third album, “Still(Leben),” arrives November 6, 2026, preceded by the singles “Bodenlos,” “Als du gingst” and “Mottentanz.”

items.title: Spankraght release ‘Killing Spree’ single
items.summary: Belgian industrial metal act Spankraght released "Killing Spree", the first single from the EP "God Please Kill Me", with an animated video.
items.fullText:
Belgian industrial metal act Spankraght released “Killing Spree” on 6 November 2026, the first single from the upcoming EP “God Please Kill Me”, paired with an animated video.

“Killing Spree” follows the mental breakdown of someone overwhelmed by a daily stream of bad news and abuse of power. Bandleader Kevin Cools recorded, produced and mixed the track and also made the video; the EP was mastered by Sven Janssens of Left Red Hand.

Cools began writing the EP’s material in the summer of 2025, shortly after Spankraght’s album “Gonflez Mon Sac”. Two months after that release, longtime bassist Wim left the band after more than 20 years playing with Cools. Cools continued the new songs alone while recruiting guitarists Jeroen Lagae and Gianni Nys for a live lineup. “God Please Kill Me” is set for release in early 2027, with further tracks and videos due in the lead-up.

“God Please Kill Me” tracklist: “Killing Spree”, “A-Hole”, “Dominatrix”, “Shooting Stars”, “Scavenger”.

“Killing Spree” is available on streaming platforms.

About Spankraght

Spankraght is the industrial metal project of Belgian musician Kevin Cools, who handles vocals, guitars, electronics, programming and the band’s visuals and live props. The project released an EP in 2018, the album “Thou Shalt Drown In The Blood Of Thy Children” in 2020 and “Gonflez Mon Sac” in 2025. For the new EP “God Please Kill Me”, due in early 2027, Cools is joined live by guitarists Jeroen Lagae and Gianni Nys following bassist Wim’s departure from the band. “Killing Spree” is the EP’s first single.

About The House Flies

The House Flies are a four-piece post-punk band from Moline, Illinois, signed to Wilhelm & Sons Entertainment Company, a label established in 2017 that also handles releases by gothic grunge band Murnau and folk act Wilhelm. The band announced “Lions and Ore” in August 2026 alongside the single “Derelict Crawl,” followed by “Lost Literature” on 2 October. “Lions and Ore,” the band’s second album, is now available in full via Wilhelm & Sons Entertainment Company.

items.title: Split Vision release new album ‘BetaCity’
items.summary: Split Vision release the album 'BetaCity' on November 6 via Town And Towers Records, drawing on the early synthpop sound of Alphaville.
items.fullText:
Swedish synthpop duo Split Vision release their new album “BetaCity” on November 6, 2026, on Town And Towers Records. The ten-track album is available on CD, vinyl and digital, and draws on the sound of Alphaville’s 1984 album “Forever Young”.

Following “Echoes of a New Spell”, which explored the early electronic sound of Depeche Mode, “BetaCity” turns to Alphaville’s catalogue as its reference point. Dan Hansson and Henric Palmqvist built the album around a Roland Jupiter-8 for lead and pad sounds, a PPG Wave 2.3 for wavetable bass, and a Linn LM-1 and LinnDrum rhythm section, with a string orchestra playing arpeggios across several tracks.

The album opens with “Shadows on the Wall”, set around divided cities and fading memories, with Berlin, Copenhagen and Stockholm named as recurring landmarks. “Cold War” follows, built on lyrics the band’s label manager, Stig Wintendorff, wrote in the 1980s about iron curtains and political tension. “Hall of Fame” and “Higher Love” move into more personal territory of ambition and regret, while “Out of Nowhere”, the album’s first single, takes a more uptempo, melodic turn. The album closes with “Drums of Freedom”, addressing war and the hope for peace.

‘BetaCity’ tracklist

  1. Shadows on the Wall
  2. Cold War
  3. Hall of Fame
  4. Higher Love
  5. Out of Nowhere
  6. Wheel of Fortune
  7. Black Crown
  8. A Split Vision
  9. Laufen durch die Straßen
  10. Drums of Freedom

“BetaCity” is available as a digital album on Bandcamp, with CD and vinyl editions available through the band’s webshop.

“Cold War”, the album’s second single, followed “Out of Nowhere” in October. Both singles carry over into the final tracklist alongside eight additional songs, including “Laufen durch die Straßen”, a track set in Hamburg in the 1980s, and “A Split Vision”, which explores a relationship breakdown.

About Split Vision

Split Vision was formed in 1985 in Kristianstad, Sweden, by school friends Dan Hansson and Henric Palmqvist, originally as a four-member high-school lineup influenced by Depeche Mode, Yazoo, Erasure and the Pet Shop Boys. The band played discotheques across northeastern Skåne in the late 1980s and appeared on regional radio programs and talent competitions. In 1988, the single “How Will I Ever” was released on Platinum Records, followed by the minor Swedish hit “So Many Times”. The group split up shortly after.

Hansson and Palmqvist revived Split Vision in 2019. Their comeback album, “Among the Stars”, released October 1, 2020, built its lyrics and soundscapes around a cosmos theme. Describing that period, the band stated: “We wanted to take the audience on a journey back to carefully carved arpeggios, that smell of Moog and Yamaha DX-7. We try to create music with an atmosphere consisting of strong melodies performed by a distinct lead and backed by a contemporary vocoder. The goal was, as far as possible, to recreate the sound we loved at the beginning of our electronic music career – and we believe, we succeeded.”

Split Vision signed to Town And Towers Records in 2022 and released an EP in January 2025, followed by the covers EP “A Trip Down Memory Lane” in May 2025. Their album “Echoes of a New Spell” followed on February 5, 2026, and the band discussed their approach to influence in a Side-Line interview published that March.

In August 2024, Norwegian filmmaker Øystein Thorsen directed the music video for Split Vision’s single “Lust”, which went on to screen at the New York Tri-State International Film Festival, the LIFF Luleå International Film Festival in Sweden, the Tokyo Short Film Festival, the KHIFF Krimson Horyzon International Film Festival in India and the Greece International Film Festival. “BetaCity” is Split Vision’s first album to be released on streaming, CD and vinyl simultaneously, following the singles “Out of Nowhere” and “Cold War” earlier in 2026.

items.title: One Must Forget – Pillars Of Shame (Digital/Vinyl Album – Ant-zen)
items.summary: Here we welcome the debut album from the Polish-French duo One Must Forget. For this...
items.fullText:
Here we welcome the debut album from the Polish-French duo One Must Forget. For this release, MK (Michał Kiełbasa) and vocalist EA draw inspiration from profound human—and, above all, psychological—processes, exploring the consequences of guilt and the paths it can lead us down.

Musically, the project evokes an Experimental approach reminiscent of the early 1980s, with strong echoes of SPK. This is far more than a mere reference; it is a genuine compliment. The album is varied, at times sounding somewhat archaic or improvised, yet it maintains a consistent underlying thread throughout. There is extensive experimentation and manipulation of sounds and effects, layered with Industrial textures and a dark, almost tormented Ambient atmosphere that borders on the Cinematic genre. The vocal elements, while never taking centre stage, add an essential dimension to the overall production.

I particularly appreciate the record’s vintage quality, which transports me back to the magic of the early 1980s. (Rating:7).

Listen to “Nature Of Mankind”:

About One Must Forget

One Must Forget is a Polish and French project fronted by Michał Kiełbasa, who also records as Neithan and works out of Tarnowskie Góry in southern Poland. Kiełbasa is active across several other projects: Whalesong, the experimental band he formed in 2009 that mixes sludge, doom, noise rock and post-punk; Lugola, his noise and power-electronics solo project started in 2012; and Harmony of Struggle, a power-electronics project he founded in 2020. “Pillars of Shame,” made with vocalist EA, is the duo’s debut release under the One Must Forget name.

Side-Line first reported the album’s release in July 2026: the record came out digitally on 18 June 2026 through the German label Ant-Zen, founded in 1994 by Stefan Alt, and followed on a limited vinyl edition of 100 copies, pressed with ten of the twelve digital tracks.

items.title: Red Cell – Collide And Combine
items.summary: Swedish synth pop in a nutshell: With “Collide and Combine”, Red Cell deliver a catchy, multi-layered masterpiece featuring deep baritone vocals.
items.fullText:
Analogue roots, a modern beat

Right from the very first second, Red Cell’s fant­ast­ic new song com­pletely cap­tiv­ates me. Sonically, the track reminds me fas­cin­at­ingly of greats such as Erasure and the Pet Shop Boys, though enhanced by express­ive, deep bari­tone vocals. “Collide and Combine” is extremely catchy, yet reveals a finely woven depth with every listen. Subtle effects and fresh sounds are hid­den through­out, keep­ing the track con­sist­ently engaging.

In their “The Red Cell Manifesto”, the band emphat­ic­ally stresses that they are not chas­ing any fixed style or spe­cif­ic era. Personally, how­ever, I see abso­lutely noth­ing wrong with allow­ing form­at­ive influ­ences to be so clearly felt in one’s own sound. To my ears, Red Cell simply sounds unique enough for that.
