items.title: Cosey Fanni Tutti at 75: the art of refusing to conform
items.summary: Cosey Fanni Tutti, co-founder of Throbbing Gristle, turned 75 on 4 November 2026. A look at her five-decade career in music, performance and writing.
items.fullText:
Happy 75th birthday to Cosey Fanni Tutti – musician, performance artist, writer, co-founder of Throbbing Gristle and one of the most uncompromising creative figures in the history of industrial music.

Born on November 4, 1951, in Hull, England, Cosey Fanni Tutti has spent more than five decades challenging the boundaries between music, performance, sexuality, identity and artistic freedom. Her career is a remarkable demonstration of what happens when an artist refuses to separate personal experience from creative expression.

Her earliest experiments with COUM Transmissions, beginning in 1969, confronted audiences with ideas that conventional artistic institutions were often reluctant to accommodate. By treating her own body, experiences and work within the sex industry as artistic material, Cosey questioned the mechanisms through which women were represented, consumed and judged. The resulting performances and exhibitions were provocative, certainly, but their impact extended well beyond shock value. They demanded that audiences reconsider who controls an image, who assigns its meaning and who has the authority to define art.

From COUM Transmissions to Throbbing Gristle

In 1976, alongside Chris Carter, Genesis P-Orridge and Peter Christopherson, she established Throbbing Gristle, the collective that would fundamentally alter the vocabulary of experimental electronic music. That October, COUM Transmissions’ notorious “Prostitution” exhibition at London’s Institute of Contemporary Arts, accompanied by a performance by Throbbing Gristle on October 18, provoked outrage in the British press and Parliament. Conservative MP Nicholas Fairbairn famously denounced the artists as “wreckers of civilisation.”

Fifty years later, the phrase sounds rather more like an accidental compliment.

Throbbing Gristle’s confrontation with established musical structures helped create the foundations of industrial music. Cosey’s guitar, cornet, voice and unconventional approach to performance were integral to a sound that rejected the comfortable distinction between musical expression and disturbing experience.

But reducing her achievements to Throbbing Gristle would overlook much of her artistic journey.

About Cosey Fanni Tutti

Following the group’s original dissolution in 1981, her partnership with Chris Carter developed into Chris & Cosey, later Carter Tutti, producing an extraordinary catalogue of electronic music that explored rhythm, sensuality, atmosphere and experimentation. Their subsequent collaboration with Nik Colk Void as Carter Tutti Void brought those instincts into a more improvisational, rhythmically driven setting.

Her solo work tells another key part of the story. From “Time to Tell” (1983) through “TUTTI” (2019) and “Delia Derbyshire: The Myths and the Legendary Tapes” (2022) to 2025’s “2t2,” Cosey has continued developing her own sonic language, moving between tactile electronic rhythms, intimate reflection and expansive experimentation.

Her writing carries equal weight. “Art Sex Music” (2017) offered a candid account of her life and artistic development, while “Re-Sisters” (2022) examined connections between her own experiences and those of electronic pioneer Delia Derbyshire and medieval mystic Margery Kempe. Across radically different historical circumstances, the book explores the determination of women to pursue their own identities despite considerable resistance.

The timing of her 75th birthday is especially meaningful. On October 18, 2026, the Institute of Contemporary Arts commemorated the 50th anniversary of Throbbing Gristle’s historic appearance at the venue, returning attention to one of the defining moments in the development of industrial culture.

Meanwhile, “Art Sex Music,” a feature documentary directed by Caroline Catz and based on Cosey’s 2017 memoir, has completed filming and entered post-production. On December 4, Mute is scheduled to release “TG24+,” an extensive limited-edition archival collection featuring 36 Throbbing Gristle live performances, newly restored and mastered by Chris Carter.

Yet Cosey Fanni Tutti’s work reaches far beyond her historical influence. Her 2025 album “2t2” is a reminder that her creative life remains active, inquisitive and intensely personal.

Perhaps her greatest achievement is that she has never allowed the past to become a comfortable artistic identity. She has continued questioning the assumptions of the very culture she helped transform, refusing to become merely a monument to industrial music’s revolutionary beginnings.

At 75, Cosey Fanni Tutti remains an extraordinary example of artistic independence: a woman who has consistently insisted on defining herself, her work and her relationship with the world on her own terms.

Happy birthday, Cosey. Thank you for the music, the courage, the intelligence and more than five decades of refusing to be conveniently categorised.

Some artists follow the evolution of culture. Others change the conditions under which culture is created. Cosey Fanni Tutti belongs firmly among the latter.

items.title: Telex share new version of ‘Twist A Saint-Tropez’ from ‘MAXI’
items.summary: Belgian synthpop pioneers Telex shared a new Maxi Version of their 1978 debut single "Twist A Saint-Tropez," taken from the album "MAXI," out 4 December 2026.
items.fullText:
Belgian synthpop pioneers Telex shared a new Maxi Version of “Twist A Saint-Tropez,” their 1978 debut single, on 3 November 2026. The track is taken from “MAXI,” an album of 13 extended mixes due on double vinyl and CD on 4 December 2026 via Mute.

“Twist A Saint-Tropez” was Telex’s cover of Les Chats Sauvages’ 1960s hit, and its original 1978 release launched the Brussels trio into wider recognition. For “MAXI,” surviving members Dan Lacksman and Michel Moers revisited the original tapes to build new extended versions, remastered and remixed while keeping the catalog’s original character.

“MAXI” also includes extended versions of “Euro-vision,” Telex’s 1980 Eurovision Song Contest entry for Belgium, and the band’s deadpan cover of Bill Haley’s “Rock Around The Clock,” which led to a 1979 Top of the Pops appearance. The album is released on double transparent red and blue vinyl and CD on 4 December 2026, with a digital edition to follow in 2027.

About Telex

Telex is a Belgian synthpop trio formed in Brussels in 1978 by Marc Moulin, Dan Lacksman and Michel Moers, among the first acts to bring electronic pop to the mainstream. The band released albums through 2006 before announcing its retirement in 2008 following Moulin’s death in the same year.

In 2021, the surviving members began a new partnership with Mute, starting with the compilation “This Is Telex,” featuring unreleased tracks alongside newly mixed and remastered catalog reissues. Telex also released a box set collecting the band’s six studio albums, and Michel Moers issued the solo single “Microwaves,” featuring Claudia Brücken of Propaganda, in 2024. “MAXI,” arriving 4 December 2026, extends that reissue campaign with new extended versions of the band’s catalog.

items.title: Magnetic Skies signs with Over The Border Records
items.summary: UK synthpop and darkwave band Magnetic Skies has signed with Over The Border Records' booking division, ahead of a third album due November 2027.
items.fullText:
UK synthpop and darkwave band Magnetic Skies has signed with Over The Border Records‘ booking division. The label announced the signing on 3 November 2026.

Magnetic Skies is a synthpop and darkwave project formed by vocalist and keyboardist Simon Kent and keyboardist Jo Womar, built around vintage analogue textures and cinematic modern songwriting. The band released its latest album, “Fragments”, in November 2025 via ReprinT.

The band said: “We’ve always wanted to take Magnetic Skies beyond the UK and build a connection with audiences across Europe, so we’re really excited to be working with Davide and Over The Border Records. Germany is a particularly interesting territory for us, and with our third album coming in November 2027, it feels like the right time to start making those connections. We’re looking forward to working together, playing some great shows and introducing Magnetic Skies to new audiences.”

Davide Pulito, CEO of Over The Border Records, added: “I’m excited to announce the signing of Magnetic Skies. I loved their sound from the very first moment so I can’t wait to book gigs for the next album promotion. Welcome on board guys!”

Magnetic Skies’ next confirmed date is 3 December 2026 at The Grace in London.

About Magnetic Skies

Magnetic Skies is a London-based synthpop and darkwave band whose lineup includes Simon Kent on vocals, keyboards, guitar and bass, Jo Womar on keyboards and vocals, and Lenin Alegria on drums. The project launched with the single “Suffocate” in June 2023, followed by the debut album “Empire Falling” that November.

The band returned in July 2025 with the single “Back To Life,” then announced its second album, “Fragments”, alongside the single “Everything’s Alright” and a run of UK headline dates. “Fragments” was released via ReprinT on 7 November 2025. With the Over The Border Records signing, Magnetic Skies is now building toward its third album, planned for November 2027.

items.title: Breathing Records releases compilation ‘Inhale Vol. II’
items.summary: Breathing Records released the compilation "Inhale Vol. II" on 30 October 2026, with 11 tracks from 13 artists including Unter Strøm, Zaatar and Sleek Teeth.
items.fullText:
Breathing Records released the compilation “Inhale Vol. II” on 30 October 2026. The album gathers 11 previously unreleased tracks from 13 artists, with cover artwork by Jesse Draxler.

“Inhale” is Breathing Records’ recurring discovery and collaboration project. Each volume follows a shared conceptual thread and spans multiple genres. “Inhale Vol. II” follows “Inhale Vol. I,” released in November 2025, and continues the label’s pairing of established and emerging acts from across industrial, darkwave and electronic subgenres.

The tracklist includes Houses of Heaven’s “Liaison,” Lavion’s “Millennial Dust,” The New Division’s “Pleasure to Yourself,” Half Joy’s “Killing the Fear,” Unter Strøm‘s “Ghost in Wires,” a Pixel Grip and MVTANT collaboration remixing “Club Mania (Snap Yo Neck),” Local Suicide and Skelesys’ “Heartbeat,” Sleek Teeth‘s “Disengage,” Zaatar‘s “Bahnsteigkante,” Void Palace’s “Set Me Free” and Snakes of Russia’s “Axe to Grind.”

“Inhale Vol. II” is available as a digital album on Bandcamp, Spotify and Apple Music.

About Breathing Records

Breathing Records is an independent label based in San Diego, California, founded in 2025 in service of avant-garde, underground, industrial and dark electronic music. The label’s “Inhale” compilation series is its core discovery and collaboration project. It brings together artists across genres and subcultures under a shared conceptual thread.

The label’s roster includes Unter Strøm, whose Breathing Records releases span the “Fragment” and “Fold” singles, the album “Between Forms,” its closing single “Stumbling,” and the live recording “Transmission 003: Live at the Breathing Records Showcase.” Zaatar released the single “Bahnsteigkante” on the label in October 2026, the same track that appears on “Inhale Vol. II.” “Inhale Vol. I,” the series’ first volume, arrived in November 2025 with contributions from Street Fever and Matte Blvck, among others.

items.title: Apoptygma Berzerk shares 1994 ‘Who Am I?’ remix of Sabotage on YouTube
items.summary: Apoptygma Berzerk uploaded their 1994 remix of Sabotage Qu'est-ce Que C'est's "Who Am I?" to YouTube on 4 November 2026, from the CD "Annorlunda."
items.fullText:
Apoptygma Berzerk uploaded their remix of “Who Am I?” by German electro-industrial act Sabotage Qu’est-ce Que C’est to their official YouTube channel on 4 November 2026. The track dates back 32 years, to a period when Apoptygma Berzerk were beginning to reach audiences beyond Norway.

Originally released on the six-track CD “Annorlunda” in 1994, the remix was produced and arranged by Apoptygma Berzerk, with Per Aksel Lundgreen credited as release coordinator.

The connection between Apoptygma Berzerk and Sabotage was not limited to a remix. On 10 April 1994, Apoptygma Berzerk played their first concert in Germany, at the Indie Market mini-festival at Kaue in Gelsenkirchen. Also on the bill that evening were Sabotage Q.C.Q.C.? and Steril.

Per Aksel Lundgreen, who was part of Apoptygma Berzerk during those early years, recalled the concert in a later interview with Belgian music website Snoozecontrol. The band also marked the anniversary on Facebook in April 2020, noting that the same day brought their first television interview, for Off Beat TV.

A further connection runs through the two acts: Sabotage vocalist Isabelle Gernand was involved in Angst Pop’s “Viva Ta Vie,” remixed by Stephan Groth and released on “Electronic Youth – Vol. 3” in 1995, with songwriting credits shared by Gernand, Groth and Lundgreen.

The remix has circulated online before, but its upload to Apoptygma Berzerk’s official channel marks the first time it has appeared there.

About Apoptygma Berzerk

Apoptygma Berzerk is a Norwegian electronic act formed in Sarpsborg in 1989 by Stephan Groth and Jon Erik Martinsen. The band’s first German concert, on 10 April 1994 at the Indie Market mini-festival in Gelsenkirchen, placed them alongside German act Sabotage Q.C.Q.C.? and Steril; Germany went on to become one of Apoptygma Berzerk’s most important markets, with a large and consistent fan base through later decades. The band remixed Sabotage’s “Who Am I?” the same year, released on the CD “Annorlunda.”

Apoptygma Berzerk has continued to revisit its back catalogue. A 25th-anniversary feature on the band’s hit “Kathy’s Song” detailed the song’s Ferry Corsten remix history, and the band’s 2022 “Black Pawn” compilation continued an ongoing rarities series. The 1994 “Who Am I?” remix, now on the band’s official YouTube channel, extends that same archival thread back to the project’s earliest years abroad.

Sabotage, the act credited on the original “Who Am I?,” has had its own more recent Side-Line coverage: the project’s four-track EP “No Bottom – No Top” is set for release on EMMO.BIZ Records in January 2027, reworking earlier Sabotage tracks including “Souvenir” and “Ewigkeit.”

items.title: Spammerheads and Azote Mental announce split LP ‘Resistencia al Impacto’
items.summary: Spanish EBM act Spammerheads and Madrid synthpunk-EBM project Azote Mental release the split LP "Resistencia al Impacto" on Caustic Records, 10 December 2026.
items.fullText:
Spanish EBM act Spammerheads and Madrid-based synthpunk-EBM project Azote Mental will release a split LP, “Resistencia al Impacto,” on Caustic Records on 10 December 2026. The album is available for pre-order as a splatter-colored 12″ vinyl, limited to 300 copies.

The split pairs four new EBM tracks from Spammerheads, based in Valencia, with five tracks from Azote Mental, including the live favorites “Deseo” and “Vidas Heladas” alongside previously unreleased material. Caustic Records describes Spammerheads as one of Spain’s leading EBM acts and Azote Mental’s inclusion as the band’s first-ever vinyl pressing.

“Resistencia al Impacto” is available to pre-order on Bandcamp ahead of its 10 December 2026 release.

About Spammerheads

Spammerheads is an EBM act based in Valencia, Spain. The band has released music through Caustic Records, including a 2022 vinyl EP. In 2025, Spammerheads collaborated with Nightcrawler on the single “Ghostless” and released the album “The Mire Chronicles,” a record informed by the 2024 Valencia floods. “Resistencia al Impacto,” the band’s split LP with Azote Mental, follows in December 2026 with four new tracks.

About Azote Mental

Azote Mental is a synthpunk-EBM project based in Madrid, Spain. “Resistencia al Impacto” marks the band’s first release pressed to vinyl, featuring the live tracks “Deseo” and “Vidas Heladas” alongside previously unreleased material, released through Caustic Records alongside Valencia act Spammerheads.

items.title: X Marks The Pedwalk’s ‘Freaks’ returns on coloured vinyl
items.summary: X Marks The Pedwalk's 1992 debut album "Freaks" returns as a limited coloured vinyl LP in the Zoth Ommog Classix reissue series, with new cover art.
items.fullText:
X Marks The Pedwalk‘s 1992 debut album “Freaks” has been reissued as a strictly limited 12″ coloured vinyl LP, with new cover artwork, as the second release in the Zoth Ommog Classix reissue series.

“Freaks” was the German industrial duo’s first full-length release, produced by Sevren Ni-arb and AL/X/S and preceded by the “Abattoir” single. The album carries the tracks “Abattoir,” “Zest,” “Repression,” “Swastika,” “Express My Sentiments Exactly,” “The Shot,” “Helpless,” “Battered Babies,” “Church for Snow White” and “Epilogue: Desert in Dawn.” It was originally released by Zoth Ommog in Europe and later issued in North America by Metropolis Records with different artwork and a longer tracklist.

About X Marks The Pedwalk

X Marks The Pedwalk is a German industrial project led by Sevren Ni-arb (André Schmechta), formed in Münster. “Freaks,” released through Zoth Ommog in 1992, was the project’s debut full-length album, recorded with original member Regan Eracs, who left after the follow-up single “Cenotaph.” The band went on to release further albums on Zoth Ommog and later Metropolis Records, including “Human Desolation,” “The Killing Had Begun,” “Meshwork,” “Drawback” and “Inner Zone Journey.”

X Marks The Pedwalk, now fronted by Sevren Ni-arb alongside vocalist Estefanía, has continued releasing music on meshwork music, including the 2022 album “New/End,” 2023’s “Superstition” and 2025’s “Insomnia,” most recently previewed by the singles “Light Your Mind” and “Bury Me.”

The “Freaks” reissue is the second entry in the Zoth Ommog Classix vinyl series, which began in September 2026 with Lights Of Euphoria’s ‘Brainstorm’ reissue.

items.title: EISGRAU releases debut single ‘Rabengesang’
items.summary: German dark rock project EISGRAU released its debut single "Rabengesang" on 1 November 2026, self-released out of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.
items.fullText:
German dark rock project EISGRAU released its debut single, “Rabengesang”, on 1 November 2026. The self-released track comes out of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania in northeastern Germany and is available as a digital single on Spotify.

EISGRAU combines cold, driving drum rhythms with dark synthesizer textures, electric guitar riffs and reverb-heavy vocals, drawing on the Baltic Sea coast and the misty forests of the region. “Rabengesang” deals with transience, inner shadows and human longing, casting the raven as a silent observer from the darkness.

About EISGRAU

EISGRAU is a solo dark rock project based in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Germany. “Rabengesang,” released on 1 November 2026, is the project’s debut single, issued independently without a label. The track was promoted to DJs and the dark music scene through the DarkTraxx mailing service.

items.title: Crá Croí releases debut album ‘Tá brón orm’
items.summary: Cork duo Crá Croí has released its self-produced debut album "Tá brón orm," an 11-track record preceded by three advance singles.
items.fullText:
Cork, Ireland duo Crá Croí has released its debut album, “Tá brón orm” (Irish for “sadness is on me”), on 30 October 2026. The self-produced, self-released record fuses post-punk atmospheres with synth-driven beats and cinematic production across eleven tracks, following eight standalone singles the duo has released since November 2025, three of them pulled from the album itself.

Crá Croí is RG and CD. RG writes, plays, produces, mixes and masters the material; CD provides vocals and painted the album’s cover artwork, and also co-produced the record. The logo is by Marc O’Grady and the crow artwork by David O’Donovan. Crá Croí describes “Tá brón orm” as “an ambitious and deeply philosophical journey” whose lyrics explore “the bleak realities of war and nuclear devastation,” drawing on 1980s apocalyptic cinema and weaving existential questions together with themes from Irish mythology.

“Tá brón orm” runs eleven tracks: “On The Fringes,” “Lord Of The Wild,” “Black Snow,” “Just Another Day,” “Sirens,” “Threads,” “Croí,” “Whispers In The Sea,” “Swords Into Ploughshares,” “Ghosts In The Bog” and “When The Wind Blows.” The album is available as a digital download on Bandcamp.

Three singles preceded ‘Tá brón orm’

Three songs from the album arrived as advance singles ahead of the October release. “Lord Of The Wild”, released 7 August 2026 and covered by Side-Line at the time, draws on the Irish myth of Cernunnos, the horned figure tied to sacred groves and ancient places. “Black Snow” followed on 4 September 2026. “Just Another Day”, issued 2 October 2026 as the album’s third and final pre-release single, puts modern life’s emotions down to performance, with authenticity swapped for what the duo call “superficial substitutes.”

About Crá Croí

Crá Croí is a duo based in Cork, Ireland, working under the initials RG and CD. RG writes, plays, produces, mixes and masters the group’s material; CD provides vocals and handles the project’s artwork and visuals, including the self-made videos that accompany each single. The duo released its debut single, “Radiation Romance,” on 10 November 2025, pairing a nuclear-annihilation theme with a motorik groove. Four more standalone singles followed: “Fires At Dawn” in December 2025, “Feeding The Fear” in January 2026, “Lost In The Electric Blood” in March 2026, and “Flesh Machines” later in the year.

From August 2026, Crá Croí drew its next three singles directly from its forthcoming album. Side-Line covered “Lord Of The Wild” in July 2026 ahead of its August release, and “Just Another Day” in September 2026 ahead of its October release. “Tá brón orm,” Crá Croí’s first full-length release, followed on 30 October 2026 with eleven tracks.

French artist Cyril Laurent has been active in the music world for over 30 years, having made a name for himself through his project Lambwool. With LMBW, he set out to explore the more Electronic side of his musical vision. Two years ago, he released the EP “Crossed Parallels”—an absolute masterpiece—and now follows it up with this eight-track album, conceived as the musical expression of a mind in turmoil.

LMBW continues along the path established on the EP, delivering highly intelligent compositions in which every track is meticulously constructed. The music resembles a sonic puzzle, with every piece fitting perfectly into the next. This is the work of a true sound architect: an artist who takes the time to craft individual sounds before seamlessly combining them with a variety of effects and rhythms. At the same time, the album carries strong Cinematic influences, thanks to its distinctive atmosphere, which leaves plenty of room for the imagination.

The album brings to mind a surgical approach to composition, with everything crafted with extraordinary precision and attention to detail. An absolute masterpiece! (Rating:9).

Listen to “Eructating”:

About LBWL

LBWL is an alias of French musician Cyril Laurent, who has recorded since 2000 under the name Lambwool. Laurent started in the early 1990s in the Marseille metal band Moon Revolution and released the 1996 EP “French Kissin” as The Soul Lives in Berlin. Lambwool’s ambient and cinematic work cites Dead Can Dance, Tangerine Dream, Labradford, Brian Eno, and The Young Gods among its influences.

The Lambwool discography includes “Fading Landscapes” in 2005 and “…And The Angel Is Gone” in 2008 on Divine Comedy Records, “Mono” in 2009, “A Sky Through The Wall” in 2012, the Nicolas Dick collaboration “Post” in 2014, and “Vanish” in 2014 on OPN, the self-released albums “Islandi” in 2018 and “Isolation” in 2020, and “Ashes” in 2025 on Cyclic Law. Laurent introduced the LBWL alias with the 2024 mini-album “Crossed Parallels” on Ant-Zen, followed by the project’s first full album, “Architecture Of Collapse,” released on the same label on June 9, 2026.

items.title: “Bury Me Alive” — DC Goth Rockers Amulet Unveil Video for “I am the Dark,” Produced by Christopher Hall of Stabbing Westward
items.summary: Bury me alive Watch my flesh decay I am the waking dead I live it every day Some mornings, getting out of bed requires a small act of impersonation. You… The post “Bury Me Alive” — DC Goth Rockers Amulet Unveil Video for “I am the Dark,” Produced by Christophe
items.fullText:
Bury me alive
Watch my flesh decay
I am the waking dead
I live it every day

Some mornings, getting out of bed requires a small act of impersonation. You face the mirror, arrange an expression, and prepare to pass among people who seem comfortably at home in their own bodies. Meanwhile, the distance between your appearance and your experience keeps growing. There is a particular loneliness in wondering whether anyone can see how badly you are struggling, especially when some part of you hopes they will. Gothic fiction has long given that estrangement a body: the creature who walks, speaks, and wears a recognizably human face while feeling separated from the living.

Washington, D.C.’s Amulet gives depression and fear a vampiric presence in I am the Dark, the first single from their forthcoming third studio album, The Dark. Produced by Christopher Hall of Stabbing Westward and released through Dist0rtion Productions, the song begins a six-single campaign.

An organ melody opens the proceedings with suitable gothic ceremony before the kick drum and a deep, insistent bassline set the body moving. That low-end momentum recalls The Sisters of Mercy, carrying the track beneath thick gothic rock guitars and sharply defined hooks. Stephanie Stryker sings with considerable authority, her delivery seductive and assertive, with a strain of hurt beneath its polished surface. The guitars bear down around her while the organ supplies a funereal flourish; the chorus lets her stretch each phrase into a forceful declaration.

The lyrics make the distance between that commanding voice and its subject especially affecting. A glance in the mirror becomes an anxious inspection: “Can they tell that I’m in hell?” Later, the smile itself becomes suspect, a socially acceptable expression concealing an experience almost impossible to communicate. Images of burial, bodily decay, and waking death give physical form to the exhaustion of continuing through ordinary days. By the repeated title, the distinction between suffering and self has begun to collapse. The darkness has become an identity, spoken aloud with enough conviction to make the admission unsettling.

The video places Amulet in a stark studio setting, its cool, nearly monochrome palette broken by pale horizontal streaks of light. Crowned and corseted, with long gloves and an extravagant black collar, Stryker holds the center as the edit cuts between the full band and close views of her face. Her gestures are expansive, her stare direct; the performance gives the song’s private distress a formidable public bearing. Brief analog-style distortion roughens the opening images, while the restrained setting leaves every glance, guitar movement, and strike of the drums exposed.

Filmed by Illumination Media at Crescendo Studios, the clip was edited and styled by Stryker. Custom garments come from Angel’s House of Design Co., with her choker supplied by Cult of Asmodeus.

Watch the video for I am the Dark below:

Led by Stryker and principal songwriter and multi-instrumentalist MJ Phoenix, Amulet bring together gothic rock, darkwave, and industrial electronics. Their live lineup includes guitarist Bob Carr and drummer Billy Holler, both appearing in the video. Following 2024’s Katharsis and the 2025 remix EP Purification, The Dark develops their interest in the supernatural as a language for emotional experience. The album arrives on April 30, 2027, through Dist0rtion Productions, on digital, CD, and vinyl formats.

A further transformation follows with I am the Dark (Stabbing Westward Remix), recasting the original’s gothic rock instrumentation through driving industrial beats and expansive synthesizers. Bandcamp pre-orders open on Friday, November 6, 2026, ahead of its full release across streaming platforms on Friday, November 13, 2026, through Dist0rtion Productions.

items.title: “Made Them Myself with Glue and Steel” — mayva Builds a Handmade Dark Fantasy in her Video for “turpentine”
items.summary: Don’t count the stars, they are not real Made them myself with glue and steel I drape the tarp you call your sky I poke the holes with needle eye… The post “Made Them Myself with Glue and Steel” — mayva Builds a Handmade Dark Fantasy in her Video for “turpenti
items.fullText:
Don’t count the stars, they are not real
Made them myself with glue and steel
I drape the tarp you call your sky
I poke the holes with needle eye

The stars seem reassuring—until someone admits they put them there. Behind the constellations are wire, glue, and a person trying to make the dark more bearable. Art offers this curious arrangement: one person builds a small, convincing shelter; another gets to rest beneath it. And the one holding the needle may still be struggling to breathe.

New York songwriter mayva follows that uneasy exchange through turpentine, the second single from her forthcoming debut album, the most difficult flower. Released November 4 and co-produced with Ethan Williams of Brooklyn’s Shower Curtain, it is, in her words, “a love letter to the strange devotion of making things.” That devotion has its costs. “Bedazzling my lungs / to make the breathing bearable” turns decoration into a desperate repair job, while each new discovery leaves her knowing less about herself. The work changes the person who began it.

For its accompanying video, premiering here, mayva takes that idea to the worktable. She directs and co-edits with cinematographer Yuri Bong, filling the film with handmade costumes, props, masks, and claymation. We move from a cramped workspace to a miniature bedroom with a tiny radiator, curtained window, and elaborate dressing table, then out to a parking lot where a huge, rust-brown creature makes the asphalt feel like the outskirts of an enchanted forest. Scale keeps shifting, and familiar objects acquire unexpected company. You can almost feel the materials between your fingers.

The video’s fondness for odd creatures and physical invention calls up that extraordinary ’80s run of dark fantasy: The Dark Crystal, Labyrinth, Legend, The NeverEnding Story, Return to Oz, Dragonslayer, The Company of Wolves, and Time Bandits. Around them sit the cursed romance of Ladyhawke, the Arthurian excess of Excalibur, the creatures of Willow and Clash of the Titans, and the animated enchantments of The Secret of NIMH, The Black Cauldron, and The Last Unicorn. Beauty and danger shared the same room; a marvelous escape could come with something capable of biting.

Another particularly apt relative is Alice, the 1988 surrealist dark fantasy film written and directed by Jan Švankmajer. His collision of live action and stop-motion animation gives ordinary objects a disobedient, sometimes threatening life. mayva’s little rooms and animated figures invite a similar attention to the things themselves: their surfaces, their proportions, the oddness of watching something made by hand begin to move. The small irregularities encourage you to look closer, keeping the human effort visible inside the illusion.

Eventually, the film carries that strangeness onto a small stage dressed for “Night Under the Stars,” where tinsel brushes the effects pedals and masked musicians look ready for a school dance with an unusually permissive admissions policy. Williams appears as the ogre, Grace Goss plays the snail, and Poncho plays Poncho. There are prom photographs, blue-lit faces, and a homemade sky hanging over the band. Those stars bring the lyrics’ reassurance into view: someone has taken the trouble to build a place where these creatures can belong.

Guitars swoop and saw through turpentine, setting mayva’s gently sung melody against the weight of early-’90s indie rock. The Sundays and Mazzy Star come to mind in the sweetness and unhurried phrasing, while the heavier passages recall Sonic Youth in their late-’80s and early-’90s balance of melody and abrasion. As the mix grows denser, the song moves further into shoegaze, with each thickening layer adding pressure around the voice.

Around two minutes and twenty seconds in, a pared-down kick-drum pattern and blunt guitar thumps open space for a more spoken-sung delivery. The shift puts the words closer to the listener, as though mayva has stepped away from the band to explain how she built the ceiling. When the guitars cloud over again, their blurred sweetness recalls My Bloody Valentine before Loveless.

Watch the video for turpentine below:

After five years performing with New York’s all-girl rock band Homade, mayva brings her poetry-led songwriting into a solo debut spanning shoegaze, dream pop, and grunge. Co-produced with Williams, the nine-song the most difficult flower begins with a winter storm and follows its aftereffects through destruction and renewal. The album is due January 15, 2027.

items.title: In Retrograde release new demo ‘Cold Read’
items.summary: Sacramento band In Retrograde released the five-track demo "Cold Read" on Bandcamp on October 12, 2026, a name-your-price digital album.
items.fullText:
Sacramento, California band In Retrograde released the five-track demo “Cold Read” on Bandcamp on October 12, 2026. The release pairs two newly mixed older songs with two newer tracks and closes on the title cut.

The tracklist runs: “Shattered Sun (2026 mix)” (3:38), “Man Love” (2:46), “Italian Disco (2026 mix)” (3:29), “Italian Disco II” (3:52) and “Cold Read” (4:10).

“Cold Read” is available as a name-your-price digital album on Bandcamp, with a $5 minimum.

About In Retrograde

In Retrograde is a goth and post-punk band from Sacramento, California. The band’s earliest release on its own Bandcamp page is the album “Aries,” from January 2019. “Californian Misery” came out in October 2020. The single “Italian Disco” followed in September 2022, and the album “Strait of Messina” arrived the next month. “The Lovers” came out in April 2023, then “Samsara/Dharma” in March 2024.

items.title: Machine Command release ‘Uncontrolable’ ahead of 2027 album
items.summary: Rotterdam EBM duo Machine Command released "Uncontrolable" on 2 November 2026, a two-track single previewing an untitled album due spring 2027.
items.fullText:
Rotterdam EBM duo Machine Command released “Uncontrolable” on 2 November 2026, a two-track digital single that precedes an as yet untitled album scheduled for spring 2027.

Annemarie Janssen wrote the lyrics and Pieter Winkelaar the music. The duo describes the title track as a piece about machine intelligence turning on its makers: “It’s about conceited self-assured and self learning beings who threaten to wipe out humanity.”

The B-side is a remix of the album track “Predators” by The Peoples Republic Of Europe. The source track runs at 165 BPM, and the remixer moved it out of EBM tempo entirely. Machine Command stated that The Peoples Republic Of Europe “transformed the fast paced EBM to Drum& bass!”

“Uncontrolable” runs 4:30 and the “Predators” remix 3:50. Both tracks are available as a digital single on Bandcamp. The cover photo is credited to Ionut and the artwork design to Design Tiger Design.

About Machine Command

Machine Command formed in 2013 in Rotterdam, The Netherlands, as a duo playing EBM. The project lists KRAT on electronics and JAANSEN on vocals.

The duo has built a long run of self-released digital titles through Bandcamp, among them “Tetrarchy E.P.”, “To The Point”, “Without Fear EP”, “New Socialism”, “Not Doing It”, “Stampfbereit”, “Without Fear V2.0”, “Two Point Zero”, “Die Rote Linie”, “Decline and Rise Again”, “Nuke It from Orbit”, “Cathected” and “Rage”. Side-Line covered the band in November 2024 when they issued the Machine Command present EBM infested ‘Affected’ album, the release that preceded the current run of singles.

The remixer on the new B-side has his own history in Side-Line’s pages. The Peoples Republic Of Europe appeared on the site in August 2013 with the New ‘Feel The Power’ album by The Peoples Republic Of Europe out now item.

“Uncontrolable” is the second single the duo has drawn from those album sessions.

items.title: Liars share ‘Beat Creep Some Eyes’ video
items.summary: Liars released a video for "Beat Creep Some Eyes", from their album "A Ban On Plastic Bag Bans", out 5 March 2027 on Mute, and set a London date.
items.fullText:
Liars released a video for “Beat Creep Some Eyes”, the latest track from their forthcoming eleventh studio album, “A Ban On Plastic Bag Bans”, due 5 March 2027 on Mute.

The video was shot by visual collaborator Clemens Habicht on an obsolete 3D camera in and around Kalamazoo, Michigan, the city that inspired the album, after Angus Andrew relocated there with his family. Discussing the track, Andrew said: “Sometimes I think the strangest thing isn’t that the world is absurd, but how quickly we get used to it. You can find yourself living inside something completely ridiculous and, after a while, it just becomes Tuesday.”

Liars announced “A Ban On Plastic Bag Bans” in September; “Beat Creep Some Eyes” follows lead track “Ice Pick, Kalamazoo” as the second piece of music shared from the record. The album was written and recorded between the United States and Australia, where Andrew now lives, with Laurence Pike and Cameron Deyell, both collaborators on 2021’s “The Apple Drop”.

Liars also confirmed a London show at Village Underground on 15 May 2027, with tickets on sale from 10am on 6 November. The band play Drum’s Not Dead 20th-anniversary shows at Phoenix Central Park in Sydney on 26 and 27 November 2026.

“A Ban On Plastic Bag Bans” tracklist: “Happy Or Not”, “Ice Pick, Kalamazoo”, “Laced Plume”, “Urgent As Always”, “Deep Deeper”, “Disaster Tropes”, “Beat Creep Some Eyes”, “Real Time Trespasser”, “SHAME!”, “Retention Arc”, “Out Of Order”.

The album will be released on vinyl, CD and digitally through Mute.

About Liars

Liars formed in New York in 2000 around Angus Andrew. The band’s catalogue spans “They Threw Us All In A Trench And Stuck A Monument On Top” (2001), “Drums Not Dead” (2006), “TFCF” (2017) and “The Apple Drop” (2021). After “The Apple Drop”, Andrew paused making music to found the record label No Gold, before relocating to Kalamazoo, Michigan, an experience that shaped “A Ban On Plastic Bag Bans”. The album reunites Andrew with “The Apple Drop” collaborators Laurence Pike and Cameron Deyell, and is set for release on 5 March 2027 through Mute, preceded by the singles “Ice Pick, Kalamazoo” and “Beat Creep Some Eyes”.

German electro act Accessory opened pre-orders on 4 November for “Outrun The End”, a nine-track vinyl collection due 27 November 2026 through Infacted Recordings, pressed in a limited edition of 200 copies worldwide.

“Outrun The End” draws nine tracks from Accessory’s catalogue, including “Dark Gothic Queen,” “Outrun the Gun,” “Deadline” and “No Man Covers.” The B-side opens with Feindflug’s remix of “War of Emotions.”

Tracklist:

Side A: “Dark Gothic Queen,” “Outrun the Gun,” “Deadline,” “Shout It Out,” “No Man Covers”

Side B: “War of Emotions” (Feindflug remix), “What The Hell,” “Bad Conditions,” “Lifesaver”

“Outrun The End” is available as a black 12″ vinyl pressing through Infacted Recordings.

About Accessory

Accessory’s history goes back to 1994, when Dirk Steyer and Kay Resch started the project in Chemnitz, Germany, under the name Voices of Darkness. Two years later, they renamed the project Accessory. Over the following decades, the duo released albums including “Jukka2147.de” (2001), “Titan” (2003), “More Than Machinery” (2008) and “Elektrik” (2019), sharing stages with acts such as And One and Hocico. “Outrun The End” brings together nine tracks spanning that catalogue on a limited vinyl pressing through Infacted Recordings.

items.title: Seances share video for Assemblage 23’s remix of debut single ‘Fade’
items.summary: Milwaukee post-punk band Seances release a video for "Fade (Assemblage 23 Rmx)", Tom Shear's remix of their debut single, directed by Kyle Arpke.
items.fullText:
Milwaukee post-punk band Seances have released a video for “Fade (Assemblage 23 Rmx)”, Tom Shear’s remix of their debut single “Fade”, retitled “Killing Karma” for the clip. The remix came out on Bandcamp on 31 October 2026; the video, directed and edited by Kyle Lloyd Arpke with artwork by Ashley Altadonna of Tall Lady Productions, follows now.

Seances is the project of Eric Arsnow (vocals, bass, guitar, drums, programming) and guitarist Jason Kartz, who helped develop “Fade” from Arsnow’s initial sketches; Dexter and Paxton Arsnow contribute backing vocals. Arsnow formed Seances after seeing The Chameleons play in Milwaukee in 2023, and cites The Cure and Joy Division as influences alongside the Metropolis, Wax Trax! and Cleopatra label compilations. Shear’s remix, as Assemblage 23, adds an electronic layer to the band’s post-punk arrangement of “Fade”.

Arsnow described working with Shear on the remix: “Being able to work with Assemblage 23 on this remix of Fade was a dream come true.”

“Fade” first appeared on Seances’ debut album “Power Is A Phantom”. The band’s live line-up draws on members with ties to The Promise Ring, Masked Intruder, Tigernite, Fight Dice and BvsMV, and a second album, “Silent Salvation”, is planned for 2027. On 23 October 2026 the band released “Tame”, a name-your-price Bandcamp track dedicated to Arsnow’s late friend Francisco Ramirez, with proceeds passed to a fundraiser for Ramirez’s daughter.

About Seances

Seances are a post-punk band from Milwaukee, Wisconsin, formed by Eric Arsnow after seeing The Chameleons perform in the city in 2023. Arsnow writes and records as the project’s core member, playing vocals, bass, guitar, drums and programming, with guitarist Jason Kartz contributing to arrangements including “Fade”, and Dexter and Paxton Arsnow on backing vocals. The band’s sound draws on The Cure and Joy Division, filtered through the Metropolis, Wax Trax! and Cleopatra label compilations Arsnow grew up listening to. Seances released their debut single “Weighted” in January 2025 ahead of their debut album “Power Is A Phantom”, which includes “Fade”. A second album, “Silent Salvation”, is due in 2027. The band’s live members have previously played with The Promise Ring, Masked Intruder, Tigernite, Fight Dice and BvsMV. The “Fade (Assemblage 23 Rmx)” video, released under the title “Killing Karma”, marks the band’s first collaboration with Tom Shear’s long-running electro-industrial project Assemblage 23.

items.title: Nightcrawler and Carmilla Sioux release ‘System Lies’ single and video
items.summary: Nightcrawler and Carmilla Sioux release "System Lies", the second single from Nightcrawler's forthcoming album "Uranium 235", with a video he directed.
items.fullText:
Spanish dark synth producer Nightcrawler and Barcelona-based DJ and producer Carmilla Sioux have released “System Lies”, a single combining industrial EBM with dark electro. It is the second single taken from Nightcrawler’s forthcoming album “Uranium 235”, out now on Bandcamp, backed by a music video Nightcrawler directed himself.

Nightcrawler produced, mixed and mastered “System Lies” at his own NC Sound Studio; the cover was designed by George Gold Design. The video places the two artists’ industrial EBM sound inside a dystopian setting of military formations, decaying apartment blocks and hospital corridors, with a control-room monitor reading “REACTOR 4, CRITICAL FAILURE” and graffiti spelling out the track’s title.

“System Lies” follows Nightcrawler’s digital album “Malevolent Forces” and his 2025 collaboration with Spammerheads, “Ghostless”. Carmilla Sioux, a former post-punk bassist now working across EBM, electro, new beat, Italo and acid house, founded the label and event platform From Hell To Disco in 2024 and also records as half of the duo Villanelle alongside Jessica Bellomo, focused on 1980s-rooted dark synth and new wave.

About Nightcrawler

Nightcrawler is the solo project of a Spanish producer who began making music in 2011, drawing on horror and science-fiction film scores for his sound. His album catalogue includes “Metropolis”, “Beware of the Humans” and “Visionary”, alongside the EPs “Perverse Frequencies” and “Dynamics of a Crash”. He has recorded with Antoni Maiovvi, Makeup & Vanity Set and S Y Z Y G Y X, and has played live at Primavera Sound and Eufònic. Side-Line previously covered his digital album “Malevolent Forces” and his 2025 single “Ghostless” with Spammerheads. “System Lies” is the second preview of his forthcoming album “Uranium 235”, pairing him with Carmilla Sioux, a Barcelona producer and DJ who has played Urban Spree in Berlin, KHIDI in Tbilisi, Moog in Barcelona and the Grauzone festival.

items.title: “Hold Me Close in The Quiet Flame” —  Cork Post-Punk Duo Crá Croí Shares Visions From Irish Mythology and a Bleak Future in “Tá brón orm”
items.summary: Hold me close in the quiet flame Through shadowed paths I hear your name An ancient grove and a city emptied by catastrophe can provoke much the same unease: the… The post “Hold Me Close in The Quiet Flame” — Cork Post-Punk Duo Crá Croí Shares Visions From Iri
items.fullText:
Hold me close in the quiet flame
Through shadowed paths I hear your name

An ancient grove and a city emptied by catastrophe can provoke much the same unease: the sense that human lives have passed through a place without entirely leaving it. Voices carry across the water, footsteps return through the reeds, and the ground seems to retain the presence of its dead. The Irish mythological imagery of Cork duo Crá Croí‘s debut album, Tá brón orm—Irish for sadness is on me—finds a troubled tenderness in these encounters. Its groves and bogs hold the possibility of reunion alongside the danger of following something beyond the familiar world.

Set those images beside the apocalyptic imagination of the 1980s, and the distance between an ancient burial place and a ruined street begins to narrow. Both confront the living with traces of people they can no longer reach. Nuclear destruction brings that estrangement into ordinary rooms: a kettle, a pair of curtains, instructions promising protection when protection has become impossible. The dread lies in the persistence of familiar things after their meaning has changed. A forest that calls someone home and a house that can no longer shelter its occupants ask related questions about belonging, mortality, and the promises people need to believe.

Across these eleven songs of Tá brón orm, the desire to feel something real, hold another person, or find a way home survives amid the images of ash and ancient ground. Beauty carries an element of danger, while affection offers a reason to keep moving toward an uncertain future. Crá Croí gives that tension melodic form, setting repeating synth figures and resonant guitars around a voice capable of both intimate address and expansive release.

Released independently on October 30, 2026, the album was produced entirely by the duo. RG takes charge of the music, lyrics, instruments, drum machines, production, mixing, and mastering, while CD lends vocals, co-production, and the album’s hand-painted cover. Their post-punk, new wave, and darkwave arrangements turn on memorable melodic motifs, with guitars and synthesizers often merging into a single, elusive texture. Against that cool electronic precision, CD’s voice shifts from deep crooning to fervent singing and measured spoken passages.

Post-Punk.com previously followed the band’s five standalone singles: Radiation Romance, Fires At Dawn, Feeding The Fear, Lost In The Electric Blood, and Flesh Machines. Those songs preceded the album’s new material, introduced by the singles Lord Of The Wild, Black Snow, and Just Another Day. Across the full-length, the duo’s growing confidence comes through in the patient development of their arrangements and the ease with which their hooks move between genres.

Snare splashes and Kraftwerk-like synth ripples open the album’s first track, On The Fringes, giving way to kick drums and an icy synthpop melody with a touch of giallo cinema. That recurring figure carries the arrangement as CD’s deep darkwave croon enters, with guitar textures adding detail around the vocal hooks. The opener introduces Crá Croí’s expanding musical vocabulary, moving freely among new wave, post-punk, and darkwave through its catchy, melodic construction. Its lyrics search for authentic feeling amid coded routines and rigid rules, bringing a restless questioning to the song’s inviting surface.

Synth sighs spread over deep drumbeats as Kraftwerkian tones give Lord Of The Wild a synthwave cast. A melodic guitar figure enters before heavier guitar textures broaden the arrangement, accompanying CD’s rich, sonorous vocals. His delivery joins new wave melody to post-punk gravity, carrying the unabashed passion of the 1980s. That emotional generosity suits the lyrics’ ancient voices, sacred groves, and wandering king called home. The yearning reaches toward the natural world, seeking a connection with something older than the machinery surrounding it.

Metallic synth tones and sizzling percussion introduce Black Snow, with a short guitar melody supplying an anxious edge. A heavier guitar revs up before the drumbeat lands, setting fuller textures against more melodic figures. The vocals enter as the synth melody chimes through the arrangement. The song’s depth comes through in both the instrumental interplay and its thoughtful treatment of loss, with images of a devastated world accompanying a persistent search for light. The melody gives that search a direction through the surrounding ruin.

Rapidly repeated notes in a deeper synth register meet chiming tones at the beginning of Just Another Day. A few recurring guitar strums hold the introduction together until the beat kicks in, sending guitar melodies circling around the synthesizers. Those lines continually work off one another, giving the arrangement a distinctly new wave character. CD delivers another strong vocal performance, with apparent doubling lending his voice a chorus effect. The melodic exchanges accompany a biting account of counterfeit beauty, borrowed feeling, and daily routines that continue even as belief in them wears thin.

Over sighing synths, a rich, resonant guitar melody gives Sirens the feeling of a cool dawn. Once the drumbeat hits, the synthesizers surge into the melody introduced by the guitar, while heavier guitar textures support it from below. CD’s vocals rise euphorically through the arrangement, holding notes with an expansive, uplifting force. That exhilaration gives the lyrics’ irresistible call toward dangerous waters a persuasive musical counterpart: the melody makes the attraction easy to feel, even as the words lead toward the breakers.

Melodic, Kraftwerkian synth tones rise and fall through Threads, their slightly bassy colouring lending the opening a baroque character. The drumbeat and guitar textures enter beneath CD’s spoken-word delivery, which sets out the scene of devastation before turning to singing as the images of blurred faces appear. Around ninety seconds in, what sounds like a minimal guitar figure begins accenting his sung phrases, although guitar and synthesizer become increasingly difficult to distinguish. The arrangement cools around the two-minute mark: sighing synths surround the more prominent beat, accompanied by a deeper tone whose source remains ambiguous. Spoken vocals return, while the exceptionally catchy synth melody connects these changes through the song’s account of hunger, destruction, and isolation.

A strong drumbeat and deep bass guitar give Croí a Floodland-era Sisters of Mercy weight, with sizzling percussion beneath a higher, resonant guitar accent. Sighing synths introduce another Kraftwerkian melody with a baroque inflection, drawing guitars and electronics into an absorbing exchange. The production blends their tones so closely that individual sources can be difficult to distinguish. That repeating synth figure holds the arrangement together as low, sustained guitar stabs accent its emotional turns. CD’s chorus-treated vocals carry considerable pathos, particularly in his delivery of “Hold me close in the quiet flame”. The phrase sends a chill through the song, holding darkness and uplift together through the sheer passion of his singing.

Whispers In The Sea takes its time reaching the vocal, opening with rich, sustained guitars reverberating over lightly sizzling percussion. A kick drum establishes a heartbeat beneath the synthwave melody and sighing pads, while what sounds like bass guitar hums underneath. Hi-hat splashes suggest waves meeting the shore throughout the extended introduction. The instrumental lines feel more distinct here, with delayed guitar notes resonating against the synthesizers, their exchanges giving the music an oceanic breadth. CD’s rich, sonorous singing suggests a solitary figure looking out to sea and beyond it toward the horizon. The lyrics’ wish to be carried home, to recover a bond with what has been lost, suits this peaceful and uplifting contemplation.

Reverb gives the baroque, Kraftwerkian synth melody of Swords Into Ploughshares an expansive reach. Sighing pads, sizzling percussion, deep bass, and weighty drums gather around the figure, with a firm rhythmic emphasis keeping the arrangement moving. The melody maintains a measured pace, allowing its appeal to develop through repetition. CD enters with something of a prog-rock serenade, his singing settling naturally into the dreamy production. Just beyond two minutes, he switches to spoken words over the synth melody and beat before returning to the earlier sung delivery. His phrasing brings to mind the poetic singing of an Irish pub: a voice holding the room through the telling of a tale. That intimate quality gives the lyrics’ reflections on war, peace, and personal absence a conversational gravity.

Baroque, Kraftwerkian synths give Ghosts In The Bog a touch of giallo, their catchy repeating melody establishing the song’s central attraction. Sizzling drums and sighing pads surround sparse guitar tones, which recur within the synth figure until the melodies seem closely interlocked. Warm bass sits deep in the mix, supporting CD’s darkwave cadence as his delivery takes on a brighter new wave character. The synth melody holds its appeal throughout, accompanying lyrics of voices among the reeds and footsteps returning across ancient ground.

A thudding drumbeat and touches of hi-hat introduce When The Wind Blows, followed by the familiar synth tones and pads. The melody climbs and descends with the same easy appeal heard throughout the record. Lower in the mix, a bass guitar groove suggests a meeting between Peter Hook and Anka Wolbert, giving the electronics a supple foundation. CD croons the story before shifting into spoken delivery around forty-five seconds in; a gentle guitar melody sits beneath his words, leading into the return of his main sung vocal. The lyrics follow people trusting instructions and familiar domestic habits as catastrophe overtakes them, with affection persisting through their bewilderment. It is a strong closing track, bringing the album’s melodic assurance and poetic delivery together.

Crá Croí is a band that keeps getting better, and Tá brón orm gives that progress room to be heard across a full album. RG’s interlocking melodies reward attention to the arrangements, while CD gives the repeated figures an emotional scale that can turn an account of devastation into an intimate address. The recurring synth vocabulary establishes a recognisable identity; the changes in guitar weight, vocal delivery, and instrumental clarity keep the songs distinct. This is a confident full-length debut, with enough feeling in its melodies to carry forward its bleakest subjects.

Tá brón orm is out now. Listen to the album below and order it here.

items.title: Covenant’s ‘The Blinding Dark’ turns 10 on 4 November
items.summary: Dependent Records released Covenant's "The Blinding Dark" on 4 November 2016. The Swedish EBM act's ninth studio album turns 10 this year.
items.fullText:
Covenant released their ninth studio album, “The Blinding Dark”, through Dependent Records on 4 November 2016, with Metropolis Records handling the North American release. The Swedish electronic body music duo’s record turns 10 this year.

Joakim Montelius described the record around release as the band’s bleakest work to date, but not a resigned one: “It’s a very dark one, probably the darkest music we have ever made. […] But it’s not a beaten, sullen darkness. It’s a defiant one.” He called the album “much more introspective” than its predecessor, the “Sound Mirrors” EP, and described the shift as consistent with the band’s approach: “Covenant’s basic principle is to always evolve: change is the only constant.”

“The Blinding Dark” runs eleven tracks: “Fulwell”, “I Close My Eyes”, “Morning Star”, “Cold Reading”, “A Rider on a White Horse”, “Interlude”, “Dies Irae”, “Sound Mirrors (Fulwell)”, “Interlude”, “If I Give My Soul” and “Summon Your Spirit”. Eskil Simonsson handled songwriting and vocals, with Montelius on programming. Daniel Myer and Daniel Jonasson joined the touring line-up on live keyboards. Dependent issued the album on CD, a deluxe 2CD edition adding a bonus disc titled “Psychonaut”, and a limited vinyl pressing, alongside the digital release.

Side-Line tracked the release through 2016: the “Sound Mirrors” EP in August, the boxset pre-order in September, and a release-week interview in which Montelius discussed the album’s tone directly. The accompanying European tour, with support from Faderhead and Iszoloscope, opened in Odense on 29 October 2016 and continued into the following spring. “The Blinding Dark” follows two other Covenant anniversary pieces on Side-Line this year, for “Leaving Babylon” and “Northern Light”.

About Covenant

Eskil Simonsson, Joakim Montelius and Clas Nachmanson formed Covenant in 1986, three friends from Helsingborg, Sweden who were then studying in Lund. They settled on the band’s name in 1988. After attending one of Front 242’s first Scandinavian shows, the trio built a studio in Nachmanson’s bedroom and began recording. “The Replicant” appeared on a Memento Materia compilation in 1992, leading to the debut album “Dreams of a Cryotank” in 1994 and the “Figurehead” EP the following year.

“Sequencer” followed in 1996, backed by a tour with Haujobb and Steril, then the “Theremin” EP in 1997 and “Europa” in 1998. The band moved labels in 1999, joining Dependent in Europe and Metropolis Records in the United States after Metropolis took over their prior US distributor’s catalogue. “United States of Mind” and the live album “Synergy” both followed in 2000, and Sony’s Ka2 division handled the European release of “Northern Light” in 2002.

“Skyshaper” arrived in 2006. Nachmanson left the band the following year and was replaced by Daniel Myer of Haujobb. The road-movie DVD “In Transit” came out in October 2007. “Modern Ruin”, released in 2011, was the first studio album with Myer as a core member. “Leaving Babylon” followed in September 2013, after the “Last Dance” EP that June.

“The Blinding Dark” arrived in November 2016, trailed by the “Sound Mirrors” single and carried on tour across Germany, Italy, Spain, Portugal, France, Greece and Finland into 2017. The “Fieldworks: Exkursion” EP followed in 2019, the year Covenant headlined the Terminus Festival in Calgary. Touring member Andreas Catjar-Danielsson died in July 2024. Covenant released the charity EP “Andreas” on Dependent Records in his memory in October 2025. Ten years after “The Blinding Dark”, Simonsson and Montelius remain the band’s core songwriting unit.

items.title: ProtoU – The Infinite Recall (Digital/CD Album – Cryo Chamber)
items.summary: With the album “The Infinite Recall,” Ukrainian artist Sasha Puzan has released her first record...
items.fullText:
With the album “The Infinite Recall,” Ukrainian artist Sasha Puzan has released her first record of the year. Over the past few years, she has been remarkably prolific, releasing an impressive number of productions, including numerous collaborations. This time, she draws inspiration from pure science fiction: a world governed by an intelligent system designed to ensure continuous improvement and prevent any form of escalation, yet one in which cracks and flaws inevitably begin to emerge.

Those familiar with this artist’s refined Cinematic style may be somewhat surprised by this album. While she remains true to what I would describe as Cinematic music, the soundscape has shifted into an entirely different dimension. The tracks possess a deep, abyssal quality and unfold gradually. They never quite reach a conventional climax; instead, they evolve organically, creating a genuine sense of movement. The album also incorporates spoken-word elements that clearly allude to AI, leaving us wondering whether the artist is encouraging us to place greater trust in artificial intelligence or, conversely, suggesting that it can never be fully trusted. Musically, she has succeeded in crafting a remarkable record that departs from the darker character of some of her earlier work, exploring a different, more mysterious atmosphere. It is a compelling achievement, not least because every track is meticulously crafted, with subtle sounds and effects adding depth and detail to the overall soundscape.

If AI as main theme can inspire artists to create music like this, then there is still hope for the future. (Rating:8).

Listen to “Achromic (A Colorless Void Where The Truth Hides”:

About ProtoU

ProtoU is a dark-ambient and cinematic project by Ukrainian artist Sasha Puzan, credited in earlier Side-Line coverage as Sasha Cats. She released the joint album “Earth Songs” with Dronny Darko in 2015, followed by her solo debut “Lost Here” in 2016 on Cryo Chamber, then the second album “Khmaoch” the same year. A collaboration with Alphaxone, “Stardust”, followed in 2017. Her most recent solo album, “Dark Orbit”, came out in 2025. ProtoU now returns with “The Infinite Recall”.

items.title: Nightcrawler and Carmilla Sioux Expose the Machinery of Deception in “System Lies”
items.summary: “Everything is under control” becomes a particularly unconvincing reassurance when the officials delivering it are wearing gas masks. Screens repeat the message, documents disappear into a shredder, and a reactor… The post Nightcrawler and Carmilla Sioux Expos
items.fullText:
“Everything is under control” becomes a particularly unconvincing reassurance when the officials delivering it are wearing gas masks. Screens repeat the message, documents disappear into a shredder, and a reactor heads toward catastrophe. In Nightcrawler and Carmilla Sioux’s video for System Lies, public relations remains a functioning department well into the apocalypse. The authorities have plenty to say, provided nobody expects any of it to be true.

The Spanish electronic producer joins forces with the Barcelona-based DJ and producer for the second single from his forthcoming album, Uranium 235. Combining industrial EBM with dark electro, System Lies examines how institutions manipulate information and conceal the truth from the citizens whose lives depend upon it.

Deep, ominous bass synths open a channel for thick industrial drums, piston pulses, with cold electronic textures hanging above the rhythm. Humming, buzzing, and murmured voices crowd the mix, suggesting messages picked up through a wall or a damaged receiver. When the beat breaks, electronic shudders take over, and a ringing tone begins to resemble an exhausted alarm. Its blurred edges leave open the possibility of a voice buried inside the machinery.

Muffled male communiques drift across the track, their words too obscured to make out. That effect suits the subject: communication continues while meaning remains frustratingly inaccessible. As the drums return, the wailing tone persists above them. Later, mechanical noises and repeating EBM-techno sequences tighten the arrangement, spiraling toward the finish with the sensation of a machine accelerating beyond its operators’ control.

Created by Nightcrawler, the clip gives those uneasy transmissions an Orwellian setting of military formations, decaying apartment blocks, and official insignia stamped across public life. Protesters ask for the truth while the state broadcasts reassurance; a control-room monitor supplies the more useful bulletin: “REACTOR 4 — CRITICAL FAILURE.” Hospital corridors, rows of body bags, and the ruined power station expose the cost of that deception. Its sickly yellow-green palette makes the whole place seem contaminated before the warning symbols appear, while burning state vehicles and “SYSTEM LIES” graffiti give the population’s anger a blunt vocabulary.

Watch the video for System Lies below:

Nightcrawler began making music in 2011, drawing on horror and science-fiction scores. Albums including Metropolis, Beware of the Humans, and Visionary established that cinematic foundation, while the later EPs Perverse Frequencies and Dynamics of a Crash pursued further electronic experiments. His collaborators have included Antoni Maiovvi, Makeup & Vanity Set, and S Y Z Y G Y X, with live appearances at festivals including Primavera Sound and Eufònic.

Carmilla Sioux brings a background in post-punk bass playing to her work across EBM, electro, new beat, Italo, acid, and techno. Her DJ appearances include Urban Spree in Berlin, KHIDI in Tbilisi, and Barcelona’s Moog, alongside Grauzone festival. In 2024, she founded From Hell To Disco, a label and event platform encompassing releases, podcasts, and curated events. She also partners with Jessica Bellomo in Villanelle, exploring dark synth, new wave, and electronic music rooted in the 1980s.

System Lies was produced, mixed, and mastered by Nightcrawler at NC Sound Studio, with cover design by George Gold Design. The single is out now through Nightcrawler Music.
